analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Three stresses hit markets at once: French sovereign stress, AI growth fears and higher oil prices. The result was a large risk-off move, with the S&P 500 down 1.21% for its worst day since July and the NASDAQ down 2.60% for its biggest decline since June.

The Franco-German 10yr spread widened 14.8bps to 174bps, its biggest daily widening since March 2020 and the highest since the November 2011 sovereign crisis. The single-currency-era peak was 189bps that month. There was no immediate catalyst, and France was the most vulnerable because it was already under market pressure.

The French moves were a risk-off pattern, not a global bond selloff. The 10yr OAT yield rose 5.8bps to a post-2002 high of 5.07% while the 10yr bund yield fell 8.7bps to 3.32%. The Italian spread to bunds widened 8.7bps to 124bps, the most since April 2025.

STOXX Banks fell 4.17% to a 4-month low, about 14% below their mid-September highs. The euro weakened 0.14% against the dollar. The yen (+0.87%) and Swiss franc (+0.48%) benefited as defensive currencies.

ECB hike pricing for December fell to 69% from 90% at Wednesday's close, which raises doubts about further hikes this year. European HY spreads widened 20bps to 369bps, the highest since April 2025, and financial conditions tightened.

AI growth concerns returned. The Philly semiconductor index fell 6.72%, its worst day since June and its lowest level since July. CoreWeave fell 10.06% to its lowest since May 2025 and its 5yr CDS widened 66bps to 1162bps.
Meta fell 6.98% and its CDS widened 7.2bps to 118bps. The after-hours reaction to its results on Wednesday had been positive, but sentiment soured on the rising capex plan.

Defensives rallied while the index fell. Consumer staples rose 3.11% and utilities rose 1.98%. Two thirds of S&P 500 constituents moved higher, and the equal-weighted index outperformed the cap-weighted index by 0.77%, the most since July 2024.

Brent closed at a 5-month high of $113.17/bbl (+4.00%) on fears of Middle East escalation. European natural gas hit a post-2022 high of €90.04/MWh. Drivers cited were a New York Times report that the US and Israel have plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms, and a Houthi claim of an attack on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil site.

Treasuries acted as a haven. The 10yr yield fell 16.6bps to 4.95%, its biggest daily decline since August 2024, despite strong data. Initial jobless claims fell to 194k (vs 200k expected), and the 4-week average is the lowest since September 2022.

Asian markets are down but off their lows. The CSI 300 (-0.54%) and Shanghai Composite (-1.20%) are at 15-month lows. US and European futures are roughly flat, so the selloff has not accelerated overnight.
Japan's September core CPI rose to a nine-month high of 2.1% y/y, above the BOJ target. Core-core CPI rose to 2.4% from 1.9%. The 10yr JGB yield fell 9.5bps to 2.77%.
Today's flash PMIs are a focus. A month ago the strong US flash PMIs drove a roughly 15bp rise in 2yr and 10yr Treasury yields, which is the opposite of the current mood.

risk_factors: French sovereign stress with no immediate catalyst, and a Franco-German spread near its single-currency-era peak of 189bps.
AI growth fears and rising capex concerns hitting semiconductors and AI-linked credit such as CoreWeave and Meta.
Oil escalation risk from a possible post-midterm US and Israeli strike on Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites.
Tighter financial conditions in Europe and doubts about further ECB hikes.
Energy-driven inflation persistence, with European natural gas at a post-2022 high of €90.04/MWh.
vol_and_positioning: European HY spreads widened 20bps to 369bps, the highest since April 2025. iTraxx Crossover closed at 331 (+11).
CoreWeave's 5yr CDS widened 66bps to 1162bps and Meta's widened 7.2bps to 118bps.
Defensive sectors led and the equal-weighted S&P 500 outperformed the cap-weighted index by the most since July 2024.
geopolitical: The New York Times reported that the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, which fuels speculation of escalation.
The Houthis claimed a recent attack on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil site, following a drone attack at a Saudi oil field the previous day.
Mounting stress around France drove the Franco-German 10yr spread to its highest level since the November 2011 sovereign crisis.
